summary: Stone County tower on the Ozark National Forest, reported as just being completed in June 1931; attendants named in 1932 and 1948. No source describes the site today.

facts.design: four-legged steel structure with an observers' cabin on top

staffing.status: attendant or tender, named in 1932 and 1948

events.note: A June 12, 1931 Baxter Bulletin item reports the Forest Service was just completing the tower. No completion date is given.
Francis Green is named as attendant at the Green lookout tower.
Doyle Lawrence is reported to have the position of tending the Green lookout tower.
Coast and Geodetic Survey station description of the tower. The 60.71 ft figure is the distance to the tower base, not its height.

notes_for_editor: Two sources, both reporting older newspaper items and a 1953 survey. Status and visitor access today are unknown; no source describes the site now, and the record's status and access stay unknown. The 60.71 ft in the 1953 station description is the distance from the station to the tower base, not the height, so no height is recorded. The record has no built year: 1931 comes from a June 1931 item saying the tower was just being completed. The 1934 item about a family moving near the tower is left out because it does not say they staffed it. The NHLR Arkansas register list in the cache has 29 towers and does not include Green. A search snippet for explorecalico.com describes a 1931 Green Lookout Tower, but that text is not in the cached page, so it is not used.
